metadata.title: Trust Region Policy Optimization (Schulman, Levine, Moritz, Jordan, Abbeel, 2015)
metadata.framework: policy optimization via surrogate objective with trust-region constraint
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:1502.05477. No LaTeX source downloaded.

nodes.name: Markov Decision Process (MDP)
nodes.statement: An MDP $(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, P, r, \rho_0, \gamma)$ where $\mathcal{S}$ is the state space, $\mathcal{A}$ the action space, $P : \mathcal{S} \times \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{R}$ the transition probability, $r : \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{R}$ the reward function, $\rho_0$ the initial state distribution, and $\gamma \in (0,1)$ the discount factor.

nodes.name: Stochastic policy and expected discounted return
nodes.statement: A stochastic policy $\pi : \mathcal{S} \times \mathcal{A} \to [0,1]$ mapping states to distributions over actions. The expected discounted return is $\eta(\pi) = \mathbb{E}_{s_0, a_0, \ldots} \left[ \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \gamma^t r(s_t) \right]$ where $s_0 \sim \rho_0$, $a_t \sim \pi(\cdot | s_t)$, $s_{t+1} \sim P(\cdot | s_t, a_t)$.

nodes.name: State-action value, state value, and advantage
nodes.statement: The state-action value $Q_\pi(s,a) = \mathbb{E}_{s_{t+1}, a_{t+1}, \ldots} \left[ \sum_{l=0}^{\infty} \gamma^l r(s_{t+l}) \,|\, s_t = s, a_t = a \right]$, the state value $V_\pi(s) = \mathbb{E}_{a \sim \pi} [Q_\pi(s,a)]$, and the advantage $A_\pi(s,a) = Q_\pi(s,a) - V_\pi(s)$.

nodes.name: Discounted visitation frequency
nodes.statement: The discounted visitation frequency (or state distribution) of policy $\pi$ is $\rho_\pi(s) = \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \gamma^t P(s_t = s | \pi)$, so that $\eta(\pi) = \sum_s \rho_\pi(s) \sum_a \pi(a|s) r(s)$.

nodes.name: Surrogate objective (importance-sampled advantage)
nodes.statement: Given the current policy $\pi_{\text{old}}$, the surrogate objective for a new policy $\pi$ is $L_{\pi_{\text{old}}}(\pi) = \eta(\pi_{\text{old}}) + \sum_s \rho_{\pi_{\text{old}}}(s) \sum_a \pi(a|s) A_{\pi_{\text{old}}}(s,a)$. This equals $\eta(\pi_{\text{old}}) + \mathbb{E}_{s \sim \rho_{\pi_{\text{old}}}, a \sim \pi} [A_{\pi_{\text{old}}}(s,a)]$, and matches $\eta(\pi)$ to first order around $\pi_{\text{old}}$.

nodes.name: KL divergence constraint (trust region)
nodes.statement: The trust region is defined by constraining the maximum KL divergence between the old and new policies: $\bar{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\max}(\pi_{\text{old}}, \pi) = \max_s D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi_{\text{old}}(\cdot|s) \| \pi(\cdot|s)) \le \delta$ for a step-size parameter $\delta > 0$.

nodes.name: Parameterized policy $\pi_\theta$
nodes.statement: The policy $\pi_\theta$ is parameterized by a vector $\theta \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (e.g., weights of a neural network). The trust-region optimization becomes: $\max_\theta L_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\theta)$ subject to $\bar{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\theta_{\text{old}}, \theta) \le \delta$, where $\bar{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}$ is the average KL divergence over states sampled from $\rho_{\theta_{\text{old}}}$.

nodes.name: Performance difference decomposition (Kakade & Langford identity)
nodes.statement: For any two policies $\pi$ and $\tilde{\pi}$: $\eta(\tilde{\pi}) = \eta(\pi) + \sum_{t=0}^{\infty} \sum_s P(s_t = s | \tilde{\pi}) \sum_a \tilde{\pi}(a|s) \gamma^t A_\pi(s,a) = \eta(\pi) + \sum_s \rho_{\tilde{\pi}}(s) \sum_a \tilde{\pi}(a|s) A_\pi(s,a)$.
assumptions: Two policies $\pi, \tilde{\pi}$ defined on the same MDP (DP_TRPO.1)
conclusions: Exact decomposition of performance difference in terms of advantages under $\pi$ weighted by state visitation under $\tilde{\pi}$

nodes.name: Monotonic improvement bound (penalty version)
nodes.statement: For any policies $\pi$ and $\tilde{\pi}$: $\eta(\tilde{\pi}) \ge L_\pi(\tilde{\pi}) - C \cdot \bar{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\max}(\pi, \tilde{\pi})$ where $C = \frac{4 \epsilon \gamma}{(1 - \gamma)^2}$ and $\epsilon = \max_{s,a} |A_\pi(s,a)|$. Thus maximizing $L_\pi(\tilde{\pi}) - C \cdot D_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\max}$ guarantees monotonic improvement of $\eta$.
conclusions: Lower bound on true return $\eta(\tilde{\pi})$ in terms of surrogate minus KL penalty
Monotonic improvement guarantee: if $\tilde{\pi} = \arg\max L_\pi - C \cdot D_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\max}$, then $\eta(\tilde{\pi}) \ge \eta(\pi)$

nodes.name: TRPO practical algorithm
nodes.statement: The practical TRPO algorithm solves the constrained optimization $\max_\theta \hat{L}_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(\theta)$ subject to $\bar{D}_{\mathrm{KL}}(\theta_{\text{old}}, \theta) \le \delta$ using: (1) a linear approximation to $L$ and quadratic approximation to the KL constraint, yielding a natural-gradient step $\theta_{k+1} = \theta_k + \alpha \hat{F}^{-1} \hat{g}$ where $\hat{F}$ is the Fisher information matrix and $\hat{g}$ the policy gradient; (2) a backtracking line search to satisfy the KL constraint exactly; (3) conjugate gradient to avoid explicitly forming $F^{-1}$.
conclusions: Practical policy update via constrained natural-gradient step
Monotonic improvement in practice with appropriate $\delta$
Avoids explicit Fisher matrix inversion via conjugate gradient

nodes.name: Convergence guarantee (informal)
nodes.statement: Iteratively optimizing the surrogate $L_{\pi_i}(\pi_{i+1}) - C \cdot D_{\mathrm{KL}}^{\max}(\pi_i, \pi_{i+1})$ produces a sequence of policies with monotonically non-decreasing $\eta(\pi_i)$. At convergence, $\pi^*$ satisfies the necessary KKT conditions of the constrained problem.
assumptions: Exact optimization of the penalized surrogate at each step
conclusions: Convergence to a stationary point of the constrained problem

nodes.name: Proof of the monotonic improvement bound
nodes.statement: Starting from the Kakade-Langford identity (LP_TRPO.1), bound the difference $\eta(\tilde{\pi}) - L_\pi(\tilde{\pi})$ by noting it involves replacing $\rho_{\tilde{\pi}}$ with $\rho_\pi$, which introduces error proportional to $D_{\mathrm{TV}}(\pi, \tilde{\pi})$ at each state, and using Pinsker's inequality $D_{\mathrm{TV}} \le \sqrt{D_{\mathrm{KL}}/2}$ to convert to KL. Telescope the geometric series to get the $\gamma/(1-\gamma)^2$ factor.
nodes.proof_strategy: Bounding the state-distribution mismatch via TV distance, applying Pinsker's inequality, and telescoping.
